statement: Let \(\mathcal E\) be an algebraic vector bundle on \(\mathbb P(\Xi)\), \(S=\operatorname{Sym}(\Xi^*)\), and \(M=\bigoplus_{m\geq0}H^0(\mathcal E(m))\). Choose an integer \(N>\max\{0,\operatorname{reg}M\}\). In cohomological degree \(m\), put \(R(M)^m=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb C}(\Lambda,M_m)\), with internal component \[R(M)^m_t=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb C}(\Lambda_{m-t},M_m).\] The differential is \((d_Rf)(\lambda)=\sum_i x_i f(\xi_i\lambda)\); it preserves internal degree. The tail with \(m\geq N\) is exact in degrees strictly greater than \(N\). Adjoin a minimal graded free resolution of its initial kernel, retaining these cohomological indices, to obtain the everywhere exact Tate complex \(T(\mathcal E)\). Then \[V=\ker\bigl(T(\mathcal E)^0\longrightarrow T(\mathcal E)^1\bigr)\] is a finite-dimensional graded proper module and \(\Phi(V)\cong\mathcal E\).
reconstruction: Both gradings, the regularity bound and the degree-zero kernel are supplied here; the notebook gives an abbreviated two-section-space construction. In the modern dual-module convention, \((a\cdot f)(\lambda)=f(\lambda a)\), so \(d_R\) is a degree-zero \(\Lambda\)-module map. By contrast the notebook's raw tensor formula has internal degree \(-1\) and anticommutes with the generators, although its kernel is still a graded submodule. For \(n=0\), \(\mathcal E=\mathcal O\), its raw kernel is \(\mathbb C\xi_0\) in degree \(-1\), hence is not proper. The dual free module \(\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb C}(\Lambda,\mathbb C)\) has degrees \(0,\ldots,n+1\), and is noncanonically \(\Lambda(-(n+1))\) under \(Q(a)_j=Q_{a+j}\); omitting that shift changes the answer.
fate_locator_suggestion: The notebook sketch belongs to the inverse BGG construction; compare \citet[\S~4]{bernsteingelfandgelfand1978bundles}. The explicit conventions above are \citet[\S~2, Corollary~2.4, Theorem~3.7 and the construction in \S~4]{eisenbudfloystadschreyer2003exterior}.
